scope.scopeNotesMd: This report compares the core R4 `DiagnosticReport` StructureDefinition with the R6 ballot `DiagnosticReport` StructureDefinition and related local terminology needed to interpret local bindings. Findings are limited to changes owned by `DiagnosticReport`: local elements, local reference target lists, local terminology bindings, local constraints, and local flags. Inherited changes from `Element`, `Extension`, `Resource`, and `DomainResource` are not reported as DiagnosticReport findings.
outOfScope: Inherited base-artifact changes such as `Element`/`Extension` constraint text changes, R6 `mustSupport: false` defaults on inherited elements, and `DomainResource` constraint expression changes.

The inherited `DiagnosticReport.language` binding changed from preferred `languages` to required `all-languages`; this is a Resource/DomainResource-level issue and is not counted as a DiagnosticReport finding.
SearchParameter, OperationDefinition, CapabilityStatement, profile, and implementation-guide behavior, except where local element changes imply likely downstream impact.
Detailed migration of removed or changed target resources such as `Media` and `ImmunizationRecommendation`; those artifacts need their own reports.

narrativeReportMd:
# DiagnosticReport R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. The highest-impact local changes are the replacement of `DiagnosticReport.conclusionCode` from `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference`, the `DiagnosticReport.media.link` retargeting from `Media` to `DocumentReference`, and the apparent rename of `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy` to `DiagnosticReport.study`.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 and R6 core package StructureDefinitions plus related local CodeSystems and ValueSets. It excludes inherited base-resource changes and separate artifact lifecycle questions for `Media`, `ImmunizationRecommendation`, `CodeableReference`, and search parameters.

## Main migration themes
R6 broadens DiagnosticReport to carry richer report context: new relationships, procedures, supporting information, recommendations, communication records, comparison material, and Composition structure. That is useful for R6 authoring but creates R6-to-R4 content-loss risk. Several existing R4 fields also changed wire shape or target domain, so strict validators and generated model code need explicit transforms.

## Highest-impact findings
Hard R4-to-R6 validation breaks occur when R4 instances use `imagingStudy`, `media.link` references to `Media`, `conclusionCode` as direct `CodeableConcept`, or `basedOn` references to `ImmunizationRecommendation`. R6-to-R4 risk is high for R6 `status=modified`, new content-bearing elements, and `CodeableReference.reference` values.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for clinical semantics around conclusion references, media migration from `Media` to `DocumentReference`, and whether new R6 contextual elements can be safely collapsed into R4 extensions, notes, or linked resources.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many R6 additions could only be introduced as optional elements in R6. The avoidable breaks are mostly places where an old property name or target could have been retained as deprecated, or where a choice-compatible migration path could have been used.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate reports should review the removed/changed `Media` and `ImmunizationRecommendation` artifacts, the `CodeableReference` datatype, and base `DomainResource`/`Element` changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 keeps the `DiagnosticReport` identity but introduces several local breaking changes. The top migration concerns are `conclusionCode` changing wire shape, `media.link` moving from `Media` to `DocumentReference`, and `imagingStudy` being replaced by `study`. Main uncertainty is design rationale and exact official cross-version mappings, because no official diff or rendered migration notes were supplied.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Implementations should plan for both structural transforms and semantic review. R4 data needs property-name and datatype transforms for imaging studies and conclusion codes, and target-resource review for media and `basedOn`. R6 data backported to R4 can lose new report context, new reference target domains, and the new `modified` status unless extensions or project-specific ConceptMaps are used.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable local StructureDefinition deltas: element presence, cardinality, types, reference targets, flags, and local constraints were compared directly. Confidence is medium for design intent and terminology nuance because official rendered diffs, ballot rationale, and live terminology expansions were not available.

findings.title: DiagnosticReport.basedOn no longer permits ImmunizationRecommendation references

oldState.summary: `basedOn` allowed references to CarePlan, ImmunizationRecommendation, MedicationRequest, NutritionOrder, or ServiceRequest.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 DiagnosticReport could trace an authorization or request back to an `ImmunizationRecommendation`.

newState.summary: `basedOn` allows CarePlan, MedicationRequest, NutritionOrder, or ServiceRequest; ImmunizationRecommendation is removed.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 narrows the permitted request lineage targets by excluding `ImmunizationRecommendation`.

facts.note: The R6 package also did not contain StructureDefinition-ImmunizationRecommendation.json.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct reference-target validation break for R4 instances that use `basedOn.reference` to point at an ImmunizationRecommendation. Strict validators and generated reference-target helpers can reject or no longer type that reference in R6.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If present, the lost link can obscure why a diagnostic report was produced in an immunization workflow.

justification.inferredGoal: Align DiagnosticReport request references with R6 request resources that remain in scope.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Only a partial base alternative: retain ImmunizationRecommendation as a deprecated R6 resource/target or loosen target-profile validation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The target removal is breaking for R4 reports that reference ImmunizationRecommendation, but the R6 package also lacks that resource. If the broader R6 goal was to retire that request resource, keeping the DiagnosticReport target is not a simple low-cost compatibility choice; it would require carrying cross-resource legacy surface or accepting weaker validation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept ImmunizationRecommendation in R6, at least deprecated, and left it in the `basedOn` target list for a transition. Another option would be to make the target list less constrained. Both preserve old instances but materially undermine the cleanup by either retaining an otherwise removed resource or reducing target-specific conformance.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve rare R4 references but keep a removed legacy resource visible or weaken validation for DiagnosticReport.basedOn.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles include ImmunizationRecommendation.
R6 target profiles omit ImmunizationRecommendation.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is illustrative and includes required `status` and `code`; the breaking part is the `basedOn` target resource type.

findings.narrativeMd: `DiagnosticReport.basedOn` was locally narrowed by removing `ImmunizationRecommendation` from the allowed reference target list. Existing R4 reports that trace a report back to an immunization recommendation can become invalid under R6 target-profile validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance with `basedOn.reference = "ImmunizationRecommendation/..."` can be R6-invalid. This affects validators that check `Reference` target profiles and application code generated with resource-specific reference unions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory `DiagnosticReport.basedOn` references by resource type. For ImmunizationRecommendation references, determine whether an R6 request resource should replace the reference, whether the relationship should be carried in an extension, or whether the report must remain versioned as R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The narrowing appears avoidable from a DiagnosticReport compatibility perspective because the old target could have remained while being deprecated. The supplied inputs do not show whether the target resource was intentionally removed elsewhere in R6.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Needs coordination with the separate ImmunizationRecommendation artifact analysis.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 allowed `DiagnosticReport.basedOn` to point to `ImmunizationRecommendation`, while R6 no longer allows that target and the R6 package does not include the resource. That is a real validator break for the uncommon case where a report traces to an immunization recommendation, but the path is peripheral to the usual order-to-report workflow and preserving it would require carrying a legacy resource or target in R6.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.basedOn` targets CarePlan, ImmunizationRecommendation, MedicationRequest, NutritionOrder, and ServiceRequest.
R6 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.basedOn` targets CarePlan, MedicationRequest, NutritionOrder, and ServiceRequest.
R6 package checked: no `StructureDefinition-ImmunizationRecommendation.json` is present.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises stability expectations for direct hard breaks, but this removed target appears rare and non-central for DiagnosticReport exchange, so the FMM context does not by itself make the local target removal disproportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 report with `basedOn.reference` to `ImmunizationRecommendation/...` fails R6 target-profile validation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking design would keep `ImmunizationRecommendation` in the target list, but because the resource is absent from R6 that is not a cheap local DiagnosticReport change. It would require retaining or emulating a legacy resource and validation surface.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment; the break is real, but the alternative is weaker than a normal target-list widening because it depends on a removed resource.

findings.title: DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy was removed and replaced by DiagnosticReport.study

semanticText.short: Reference to full details of imaging associated with the diagnostic report
semanticText.definition: One or more links to full details of any imaging performed during the diagnostic investigation.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented linked imaging studies in a property named `imagingStudy`.

newState.summary: `study` is an optional repeating Reference(ImagingStudy) with broader wording about studies or analyses.

semanticText.short: Reference to full details of an analysis associated with the diagnostic report
semanticText.definition: One or more links to full details of any study performed during the diagnostic investigation.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses a new property name, `study`, for the same target resource type and broadens the description from imaging to studies or analyses.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy` is absent in R6; `DiagnosticReport.study` is new, has the same cardinality and `Reference(ImagingStudy)` target, and preserves similar comments about PACS/DICOM and overlap with media.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a wire-name break. R4 JSON/XML with `imagingStudy` contains an unknown R6 element, while R6 `study` is unknown to R4. Generated models, serializers, FHIRPath expressions, search extraction code, and mapping logic must be updated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: For imaging workflows, dropping or failing to transform the link can disconnect reports from source imaging studies.

justification.inferredGoal: Generalize the element beyond imaging-specific terminology while retaining ImagingStudy linkage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy` and update its definition/aliases instead of renaming it to `study`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R6 `study` still targets only ImagingStudy and has the same cardinality. The goal appears to be clearer, more general wording, which could mostly be achieved by retaining the R4 element name with revised prose. The hard wire-name break therefore looks avoidable from the available evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep `imagingStudy` as the canonical element and broaden its short/definition to mention studies or analyses, perhaps adding `study` as an alias in documentation. Adding a second same-resource element would be another transition strategy but would risk indefinite duplicate representations; simply retaining the old name avoids that duplication.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 instances with low technical cost, but leaves a less general element name and may constrain future non-imaging study semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy` as `0..* Reference(ImagingStudy)`.
R6 defines `DiagnosticReport.study` as `0..* Reference(ImagingStudy)` and has no `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy` element.

examples.examplesMd: The transform is structurally straightforward when the target is ImagingStudy, but the property name change is still a hard validation and code-generation break.

findings.narrativeMd: `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy` is not present in R6. Its closest successor is `DiagnosticReport.study`, which keeps the same target resource but changes the element name and broadens the prose. This will surprise implementers because the data can be preserved, but only if an explicit version-aware transform is applied.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using `imagingStudy` are invalid against the R6 core StructureDefinition because the element no longer exists. Conversely, R6 instances using `study` are not R4-representable without renaming the property back.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy[]` to `DiagnosticReport.study[]` during R4-to-R6 conversion and reverse it for R6-to-R4 when all references are ImagingStudy. Update FHIRPath, search extraction, serializers, and generated model properties.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The old name could have been retained as deprecated while the new generalized name was introduced. That would have reduced validation breaks but required duplicate-element reconciliation rules.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy` was replaced by `DiagnosticReport.study` even though the observed R6 element still has cardinality `0..*` and still targets only `ImagingStudy`. Existing R4 instances and generated code break on the wire-name change, while the apparent R6 benefit is mostly a broader label and definition. For a mature trial-use diagnostic workflow, that looks like an avoidable compatibility break.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot defines `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy` as `0..* Reference(ImagingStudy)`.
R6 snapshot has no `DiagnosticReport.imagingStudy` element and defines `DiagnosticReport.study` as `0..* Reference(ImagingStudy)`.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use increases the burden to justify a wire-format rename on a clinically meaningful element, especially where the type and target did not materially change.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 JSON/XML containing `imagingStudy` has an unknown element in R6; runtime/API/codegen also breaks for model properties, FHIRPath, indexing, and transforms keyed to the old path.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A low-cost base design appears available: keep the `imagingStudy` wire name and broaden its prose to cover the intended study concept. If future non-imaging targets are needed, they could be added explicitly without renaming the existing element.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Yes alternative judgment; this remains the clearest avoidable break in the report.

findings.title: DiagnosticReport.media.link retargeted from Media to DocumentReference

oldState.summary: `media.link` was required within each media backbone entry and targeted `Media`.

newState.summary: `media.link` remains required within each media entry but targets `DocumentReference` and is no longer a summary element.

semanticText.short: Reference to the image or data source
semanticText.definition: Reference to the image or data source.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with `media.link.reference` pointing to `Media/...` no longer satisfy the R6 target profile. R6 instances point to `DocumentReference/...`, which R4 `media.link` does not permit. Because the element is mandatory inside each `media` repetition, any retained media entry must be converted rather than partially migrated.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect media migration can detach reports from clinically relevant images or supporting diagnostic data.

justification.inferredGoal: Use DocumentReference as the surviving or preferred container for report-related images and data.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain Media in R6 as deprecated and allow `media.link` to target Media or DocumentReference during transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The target replacement is a hard break, but R6 does not include a Media StructureDefinition and the DiagnosticReport text broadens to images or data. If the R6 goal was resource-model consolidation around DocumentReference, a dual-target compatibility path is only partial and carries real interoperability cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would keep the Media resource and include both Media and DocumentReference in the target profile list. That would validate R4 instances while supporting the new target, but it would also force R6 implementers to support two containers for similar facts and maintain conversion rules indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old references but conflicts with apparent Media removal and creates duplicate media/document representations that may persist.

evidence.detail: R4 `media.link` targets `Media`.
R6 `media.link` targets `DocumentReference`.
No R6 `StructureDefinition-Media.json` was found.

examples.examplesMd: The examples focus on target type. Real migration must also transform or preserve the referenced resource content.

findings.narrativeMd: `DiagnosticReport.media.link` changed target resource from `Media` to `DocumentReference`, while the surrounding prose changed from key images to key images or data. This is a major local compatibility issue for imaging and diagnostic-data workflows that used the R4 Media resource.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old `Media/...` references can be R6-invalid, and new `DocumentReference/...` references are not valid R4 `media.link` targets. Summary behavior also changes because `media.link` was R4 summary content but is not summary in R6.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Convert referenced `Media` resources to suitable `DocumentReference` resources or preserve the relationship with an extension if conversion is not lossless. Update validators, generated reference types, and summary response expectations. Test reports with multiple media entries and comments.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably tied to a broader resource-model consolidation, but it is not backward-compatible for DiagnosticReport. A compatibility period with both targets would have reduced breaks if the R6 model retained Media.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Coordinate with the separate Media and DocumentReference analyses; the safe transform depends on the content of the referenced resource.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `DiagnosticReport.media.link` moved from `Reference(Media)` to `Reference(DocumentReference)`. That is a hard local break for R4 reports with key image/media links and a reverse break for R6 reports with document references. The clinical data can be important, but R6 also removes the `Media` resource, so keeping the old target locally would require carrying a broader legacy model rather than just tweaking this element.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.media.link` targets `Media` and is required inside each `media` repetition.
R6 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.media.link` targets `DocumentReference` and is required inside each `media` repetition.
R6 package checked: no `StructureDefinition-Media.json` is present.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use keeps the clinical media-link break significant, but the missing R6 `Media` resource makes the local change look tied to a broader model replacement rather than a gratuitous DiagnosticReport-only narrowing.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `media.link` references to `Media/...` fail R6 target-profile validation; R6-to-R4 loss also exists for `DocumentReference/...` links.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Allowing both `Media` and `DocumentReference` would preserve more old instances only if R6 retained `Media`. That transitional design has material costs: duplicate media representations, extra resource support, and more complex validation/mapping.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the break is high-impact, but the less-breaking alternative is not a low-cost local base design.

findings.title: DiagnosticReport.conclusionCode changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: `conclusionCode` was `0..* CodeableConcept` with an example clinical-findings binding.

binding.description: Diagnosis codes provided as adjuncts to the report.

newState.summary: `conclusionCode` is `0..* CodeableReference` targeting Observation or Condition and still has an example clinical-findings binding for concepts.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape changes. A direct R4 `CodeableConcept` array item is not the R6 `CodeableReference` shape, where the concept is carried under `concept` or a resource link under `reference`. R6 references to Observation or Condition cannot be losslessly represented by R4 `CodeableConcept`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Conclusion or impression codes can drive clinical decision support, quality reporting, and billing; losing reference-vs-code semantics can alter interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow conclusions to be represented either as coded concepts or as references to Observation/Condition resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `conclusionCode` as CodeableConcept and add a separate optional reference-capable conclusion element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing conclusion semantics to point to Observation or Condition is a reasonable R6 goal. The less-breaking design is real, but it has material long-term costs because coded and referenced conclusions can diverge and clients must understand both representations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base R6 alternative would leave `conclusionCode` unchanged for R4 compatibility and add a sibling such as `conclusionReference` or a new CodeableReference-bearing element. That avoids invalidating old wire shapes but introduces duplicate same-resource representations of the conclusion, ambiguity about precedence, and safety-sensitive migration rules.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old code-only instances but splits one clinical conclusion across code and reference fields with reconciliation risk.

evidence.detail: R4 type is CodeableConcept.
R6 type is CodeableReference with Observation and Condition targets.

examples.examplesMd: R4 code-only content can be wrapped in `concept`; R6 reference-only content has no native R4 `conclusionCode` equivalent.

findings.narrativeMd: `conclusionCode` now carries `CodeableReference`, not `CodeableConcept`. This enables richer references but breaks old serialized content and generated property types for any implementation that populated conclusion codes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `conclusionCode[0].coding` are invalid as R6 `CodeableReference` unless transformed to `conclusionCode[0].concept.coding`. R6 `conclusionCode[0].reference` cannot be represented in R4 without choosing a code, adding an extension, or losing the link.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap existing R4 CodeableConcept values in `CodeableReference.concept`. For R6-to-R4, map `concept` back directly, but handle `reference` values with manual policy: derive a code from the target resource only if safe, otherwise preserve via extension or reject lossless backport.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The semantic goal is strong, but changing an existing element's datatype is more disruptive than adding a new reference-bearing element. A backward-compatible alternative was available at the cost of additional model surface.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The clinical meaning of references to Observation versus Condition should be reviewed in migration rules.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `conclusionCode` changed from a direct `CodeableConcept` array to `CodeableReference`, so old coded conclusions must be wrapped under `concept` before they validate in R6. The change also enables R6 conclusions to point at `Observation` or `Condition`, which cannot be represented by the old R4 code-only shape. This is clinically meaningful, but the R6 design directly supports a reasonable code-or-reference goal and old coded values have a straightforward mechanical migration.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.conclusionCode` is `0..* CodeableConcept` with an example clinical-findings binding.
R6 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.conclusionCode` is `0..* CodeableReference` targeting Observation and Condition, with the same example value set.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use makes the hard datatype break important, but the element is optional and the core R4 coded case migrates deterministically into `CodeableReference.concept`.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 `CodeableConcept` object with `coding` directly under `conclusionCode[]` is not the R6 `CodeableReference` shape; R6-to-R4 loss occurs for reference-only conclusions.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative exists: keep `conclusionCode` as `CodeableConcept` and add a separate reference-capable conclusion element. That would preserve old wire shape but creates two places for the same clinical conclusion and requires precedence/reconciliation rules.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the fresh judgment treats the break as proportionate given the R6 goal and migration path.

findings.title: DiagnosticReport.issued widened from instant to dateTime

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 required the report availability timestamp to use instant precision.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 permits the broader FHIR `dateTime` primitive, including reduced precision values.

facts.note: This is a validation widening for R4-to-R6 but a representability narrowing for R6-to-R4.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 instants are valid dateTime values, so this should not invalidate old instances. New R6 instances can use lower precision dateTimes that are not valid R4 instants, and generated code changes from an instant-specific type to a broader date/time type.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reduced timestamp precision can affect ordering, release-time audit logic, and downstream calculations.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow report issuance to be recorded when only date or partial date-time precision is known.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: changing `issued` from instant to dateTime preserves R4 instant values in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This is a type widening for R4-to-R6 instance validation: existing R4 instants fit within R6 dateTime. The likely goal of accepting lower precision is reasonable, and ordinary migration guidance or an R6-to-R4 extension is not a backward-compatible base alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No backward-compatible alternative is needed for preserving R4 instances. Keeping `instant` and adding an extension for lower precision would mainly be a backport strategy and would reduce interoperability for the new R6 capability.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 precision loss and broader generated types, not a less-breaking R4-to-R6 base-design alternative.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `instant`.
R6 type is `dateTime`.

examples.examplesMd: A reduced-precision R6 `dateTime` such as year-month is not an R4 `instant`.

findings.narrativeMd: `DiagnosticReport.issued` changed from `instant` to `dateTime`. That is not an R4-to-R6 instance break, but it is a runtime and backporting risk wherever systems assumed exact timestamp precision.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 valid instants should remain valid in R6. R6 dateTime values that omit time, seconds, or timezone cannot be losslessly converted to R4 instant without inventing precision.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve R4 instants as-is. For R6-to-R4, reject reduced precision or carry it in an extension rather than fabricating a timestamp unless a project-specific policy explicitly allows imputation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is a reasonable widening but changes the contract of the element. A less disruptive alternative would have used an extension for lower precision values.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `issued` widened from `instant` to `dateTime`. Existing R4 instants remain acceptable as R6 dateTimes, so this does not invalidate old reports. The main concern is reverse exchange or code that assumes every R6 issued value has instant-level precision.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.issued` type is `instant`.
R6 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.issued` type is `dateTime`.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not add much concern because the change is widening for R4-to-R6 validation rather than a direct break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: a new R6 low-precision `dateTime` may not be representable as an R4 `instant`; there is no R4-to-R6 instance break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base design is needed for R4-to-R6 compatibility. Retaining `instant` would avoid reverse precision issues but would also block the intended R6 widening.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse-risk rationale and Not applicable alternative judgment, but disagree with treating this as a Medium R4-to-R6 compatibility concern.

findings.title: DiagnosticReport.status required value set adds modified

oldState.summary: Required binding to `diagnostic-report-status|4.0.1`; code system lacked `modified`.

binding.description: The status of the diagnostic report.

newState.summary: Required binding to `diagnostic-report-status|6.0.0-ballot4`; code system includes new child code `modified` under `partial`.

binding.description: The status of the diagnostic report.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The ValueSets include the complete local DiagnosticReport status CodeSystem. The report compared CodeSystem concepts directly rather than using a terminology-server expansion.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No R4 status code was removed, so R4 instances should validate in R6. R6 instances using the new required-binding code `modified` are invalid in R4 and can break enum switches or status workflows that assume the R4 code set.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: `modified` distinguishes pre-final changed reports from final amended/corrected/appended reports; collapsing it can alter workflow interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent modifications to non-final reports distinctly from amendments to final reports.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `modified` is an additive R6 status code and no R4 status code is removed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding a status for changed non-final reports fills a clear lifecycle distinction while preserving all R4 statuses. Mapping `modified` back to R4 or carrying it in an extension is migration/backport work, not a less-breaking base R6 design alternative.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this is an additive required-binding expansion, R4 instances remain valid in R6. A design that used `partial` plus an extension would only preserve R4 enum compatibility for down-conversion and would make the R6 distinction less visible to generic clients.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The cost is enum updates and R6-to-R4 mapping for `modified`, not breakage of R4-valid instances.

evidence.detail: R4 required binding points to diagnostic-report-status version 4.0.1.
R6 required binding points to diagnostic-report-status version 6.0.0-ballot4.
R6 adds `modified` with definition for a modified non-final report.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative; use an official cross-version extension if one is available.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds `modified` to the required `DiagnosticReport.status` code set. This is forward-compatible for R4 data but not backward-compatible for R6 data or code generated from the R4 enum.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: `status=modified` is valid in R6 and invalid in R4. R4-to-R6 validation is not broken because no R4 status code appears to have been removed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update enum handling and status-transition logic. For R6-to-R4, decide whether `modified` maps to `partial`, is preserved in an extension, or blocks backporting.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new code addresses a real lifecycle distinction. It could have been modeled as `partial` plus extension, but that would reduce interoperability of the distinction.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds the `modified` status under the required DiagnosticReport status code system without removing any R4 status code. R4 reports keep validating in R6. R4-oriented enum switches may need updates when they consume R6 data, but that is normal additive version evolution and the new code has a clear workflow meaning.
keyEvidence: R4 `diagnostic-report-status` code system has partial/preliminary but no `modified` code.
R6 `diagnostic-report-status` code system adds `partial.modified` for a modified non-final report.
R4 and R6 snapshots both bind `DiagnosticReport.status` with required strength to their versioned status value set.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not weigh strongly against an additive code because no R4 code is removed and the new status improves expressiveness.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 `modified` is not a valid R4 status and can surprise R4 enum logic; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking alternative is needed. Avoiding the code or representing it only out-of-band would reduce computability of a meaningful pre-final modification state.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing justification and Not applicable alternative judgment, but the Medium impact overstates the forward-compatibility concern.

findings.title: Subject, performer, and resultsInterpreter reference domains were widened

oldState.summary: R4 allowed narrower target resource sets for subject, performer, and resultsInterpreter.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 subject was limited to Patient, Group, Device, or Location; performer and resultsInterpreter were limited to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, or CareTeam.

newState.summary: R6 adds multiple target resource types to these references.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 subject additionally allows Organization, Practitioner, Medication, Substance, and BiologicallyDerivedProduct. Performer additionally allows HealthcareService, Device, Patient, and RelatedPerson. ResultsInterpreter additionally allows Patient and RelatedPerson.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Target additions do not invalidate R4 instances, but R6 instances using the new targets fail R4 target-profile validation and can break applications with exhaustive resource-type switches or generated union types.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Unexpected subject or performer types can alter attribution, patient context, and responsibility workflows if backported or consumed by R4-oriented code.

justification.inferredGoal: Support broader diagnostic use cases including products, substances, point-of-care devices, and non-practitioner participants.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: subject, performer, and resultsInterpreter target additions preserve R4 target choices.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 reference-domain changes are widenings. Existing R4 references remain valid, and the goal of supporting broader diagnostic contexts is evident from R6 comments, so extensions for new targets are not backward-compatible alternatives to a breaking base change.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design is needed because the base target lists only add choices. Using extensions or profiles for the new target types would be a less interoperable R6 design and mainly addresses compatibility with R4 ecosystems.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is only for R6-to-R4 backporting and for code that assumed exhaustive R4 target unions.

evidence.detail: R4 target lists are narrower.
R6 target lists include additional resource types.

examples.examplesMd: R4 has no native target-profile allowance for these particular subject and performer target types.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 broadens several core DiagnosticReport references. This is a non-breaking R4-to-R6 model expansion, but it matters for backporting and for runtime code that assumes R4's smaller target domains.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances remain valid in R6. R6 instances with newly allowed target types can be R4-invalid and can fail deserialization or business rules that enumerate expected resource types.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit reference-type switches and generated client models. For R6-to-R4, either reject unsupported targets, carry them in extensions, or map to a supported related entity only with explicit business approval.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The widened targets are a reasonable expressivity improvement. Extensions or profiles would be more backward-compatible but less interoperable in generic R6.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Clinical and operational policy should decide whether subject types like Medication or Substance are acceptable in local workflows.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 broadens the allowed targets for `subject`, `performer`, and `resultsInterpreter`. Existing R4 references remain valid in R6; only R6-authored uses of the new target types create reverse-version or exhaustive-switch work. This is expansion, not a compatibility problem for R4 reports moving to R6.
keyEvidence: R4 `subject` targets Patient, Group, Device, and Location; R6 adds Organization, Practitioner, Medication, Substance, and BiologicallyDerivedProduct.
R4 `performer` targets Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, and CareTeam; R6 adds HealthcareService, Device, Patient, and RelatedPerson.
R4 `resultsInterpreter` targets Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Organization, and CareTeam; R6 adds Patient and RelatedPerson.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not create a stability issue because the target domains were widened rather than narrowed.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: new R6 target types may not pass R4 target-profile validation or R4 generated unions; R4-to-R6 instances are preserved.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking alternative is needed. Keeping the R4 target lists would avoid reverse surprises but would defeat the R6 goal of supporting additional legitimate subjects and actors.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing evidence and Not applicable alternative judgment, but disagree with a Medium overall concern for a target widening.

findings.title: R6 adds several optional content-bearing DiagnosticReport elements with no R4 native equivalent

affectedLocation.newPath: DiagnosticReport.relatesTo | DiagnosticReport.procedure | DiagnosticReport.note | DiagnosticReport.supportingInfo | DiagnosticReport.composition | DiagnosticReport.recommendation | DiagnosticReport.communication | DiagnosticReport.comparison

oldState.summary: R4 had no native elements for these R6 report relationships, comments, supporting information, recommendations, communications, comparisons, or composition structure.
oldState.narrativeMd: Some R4 packages include DiagnosticReport-related extensions, but the base R4 resource does not have these elements.

newState.narrativeMd: The added elements are optional for validation, but they can carry clinically or operationally important report context.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not break R4-to-R6 validation, but R6 instances using these fields cannot be represented in base R4 without extensions or external linked-resource conventions. Generated R4 clients will ignore, reject, or lose these fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Fields such as recommendations and critical communications can affect follow-up care and medico-legal audit trails if dropped.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent richer diagnostic reporting context directly in the base resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: these are optional additive R6 elements, not R4-to-R6 breaking removals or narrowings.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional elements is the normal forward-compatible way to add base R6 capability. R4 instances that omit them remain valid in R6, so the justification question is not whether an old shape could have been preserved but how to manage down-conversion loss.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: There is no backward-compatible base alternative to calibrate for R4-to-R6 preservation. R4 extensions or linked-resource conventions can mitigate backport loss, but they do not make a different R6 base design less breaking because the R6 additions themselves do not break old instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: They create R6-to-R4 content-loss risk, but extension/backport strategies are mitigations rather than base-design alternatives.

evidence.detail: These elements exist in R6 and are absent in R4.
The corresponding base R4 elements are absent.

note.text: Critical value was phoned to the ordering clinician.

examples.examplesMd: Base R4 has no native slots for these R6 fields. A backport needs extensions or external linkage rules.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 substantially expands DiagnosticReport's content model with optional elements. The additions are not hard breaks for old R4 data, but they are important migration risks because R6-authored content can be silently lost by R4 stores or clients.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is unaffected when the elements are absent. R6-to-R4 conversion is not lossless for populated new elements unless a site-specific extension strategy is used.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a backport policy for each new field. Prefer official cross-version extensions if available; otherwise create governed local extensions, preserve linked resources in a Bundle, or declare the conversion lossy. Include safety tests for recommendations and communications.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are the least disruptive way to add new R6 capability, but they cannot be made natively representable in R4 without prior extension definitions.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The clinical importance of `recommendation`, `communication`, and `comparison` makes silent data loss especially undesirable.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The listed R6 elements are optional additions. They let R6 reports carry relationships, procedures, notes, supporting information, composition, recommendations, communications, and comparisons that base R4 did not model directly. R4 reports do not become invalid or harder to read in R6 because these fields exist; the concern is only that R6-authored content may be lost when forced back into R4.
keyEvidence: R6 snapshot includes `relatesTo`, `procedure`, `note`, `supportingInfo`, `composition`, `recommendation`, `communication`, and `comparison` under DiagnosticReport.
R4 snapshot has no corresponding base elements for those paths.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not argue against optional additive content because it preserves R4-to-R6 validity and expands expressiveness.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6-only optional fields may be dropped or need extensions in R4; there is no R4-to-R6 instance break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base design is needed. Not adding the elements would avoid reverse-version loss only by preventing R6 from representing useful information in the base model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse-loss observation and Not applicable alternative judgment, but disagree that optional additions should carry a Medium compatibility concern.

findings.title: New composition element is governed by a DiagnosticReport-specific error invariant

oldState.summary: R4 had no `DiagnosticReport.composition` element and no corresponding local invariant.

newState.summary: R6 adds `DiagnosticReport.composition` and root invariant `dgr-1` with severity error.

constraints.human: When a Composition is referenced in `DiagnosticReport.composition`, all Observation resources referenced in `Composition.entry` must also be referenced in `DiagnosticReport.result` or in the `Observation.hasMember` references.
constraints.expression: composition.exists() implies (composition.resolve().section.entry.reference.all($this.resolve() is Observation implies $this in (%resource.result.reference|%resource.result.reference.resolve().hasMember.reference)))

impact.impactRationaleMd: The invariant does not affect R4 instances because the triggering element did not exist. It does affect R6 validation: a report that references a Composition must also ensure Observation entries are mirrored through `result` or `Observation.hasMember`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: If composition structure and result references diverge, readers may miss observations or display a report inconsistently.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure Composition structure does not hide Observation results from the main DiagnosticReport result graph.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: the invariant applies only when using new R6 `DiagnosticReport.composition`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R4 had no composition element, so the error invariant cannot invalidate old R4 instances. The rule serves a reasonable consistency goal by ensuring Composition observations remain visible through the DiagnosticReport result graph.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No R4-to-R6 backward-compatible alternative is needed. Making `dgr-1` a warning would be a different R6 conformance tradeoff, not a way to preserve R4-valid data; it would weaken the guarantee that structured report sections and computable results stay aligned.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Warning or profile-only enforcement would ease R6 authoring but is not an R4 compatibility alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 root constraint `dgr-1` is a local DiagnosticReport error invariant.
R4 has no local DiagnosticReport constraint corresponding to `dgr-1`.

examples.examplesMd: An R6 DiagnosticReport with `composition` can fail validation if the referenced Composition section includes Observation entries not also reachable through `DiagnosticReport.result` or `Observation.hasMember`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces `DiagnosticReport.composition` for report structure, but not as an unconstrained pointer. The new `dgr-1` invariant forces Observation entries in the Composition to also be visible through the DiagnosticReport result graph.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 break for existing data, but it is a new R6 conformance rule for authors. Validators must resolve the Composition and Observation references to fully evaluate the rule.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When creating R6 structured reports, populate `DiagnosticReport.result` or `Observation.hasMember` consistently with Composition section entries. Add validation fixtures where Composition contains observations both correctly and incorrectly mirrored.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rule could have been a warning, but an error is defensible because otherwise a structured report could be internally inconsistent.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The FHIRPath expression depends on reference resolution; implementation behavior may vary when referenced resources are unavailable to the validator.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The `dgr-1` invariant only applies when an R6 report uses the new `DiagnosticReport.composition` element. There was no R4 composition path for this rule to invalidate. The constraint requires Observation entries in the referenced Composition to also be reachable through `result` or `Observation.hasMember`, which is a consistency rule for new R6 structured reports rather than a migration break.
keyEvidence: R6 root constraint `dgr-1` has severity `error` and references `DiagnosticReport.composition`.
R6 snapshot defines `DiagnosticReport.composition` as `0..1 Reference(Composition)`.
R4 snapshot has no `DiagnosticReport.composition` element and no corresponding local `dgr-1` constraint.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not materially heighten concern because the invariant governs new optional R6 content, not established R4 content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: none: no R4-to-R6 instance becomes invalid because of this R6-only composition constraint; it is a validation rule for a new optional path.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A warning-level invariant would be less restrictive for R6 authors, but it would weaken the result/composition consistency objective and is not needed to preserve R4 compatibility.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Not applicable alternative judgment, but disagree with the Medium impact assigned to an R6-only invariant on a new optional element.

findings.title: DiagnosticReport.conclusion changed from string to markdown

oldState.summary: `conclusion` was `0..1 string` and not a summary element.

newState.summary: `conclusion` is `0..1 markdown` and is a summary element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON primitive representation is still a string-like value, so ordinary R4 conclusion text should usually remain parseable. The declared primitive type and rendering expectations change, which affects generated model types, sanitization, display, and summary payload behavior.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Conclusion text is clinically important; markdown rendering or escaping mistakes can alter what clinicians see.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `conclusion` as string and add a separate optional markdown/formatted conclusion element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R4 conclusion strings remain syntactically valid as R6 markdown, but the declared primitive type changes generated models and display obligations. Using the standard markdown primitive for the existing human conclusion is reasonable; the less-breaking sibling-element design has material duplication and safety tradeoffs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep `conclusion` as `string` and add a new markdown-capable field for formatted text. That would reduce code-generation churn, but it would leave two places for the same clinical narrative and require rules for precedence, synchronization, and safe rendering.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves generated string contracts but creates duplicate conclusion narratives and unclear rendering precedence.

evidence.detail: R4 type is `string` and `isSummary` is false.
R6 type is `markdown` and `isSummary` is true.

examples.examplesMd: Plain R4 text can be carried as R6 markdown, but systems should treat it as markdown-capable text for display and sanitization.

findings.narrativeMd: `conclusion` changes primitive type from `string` to `markdown`. This is mainly a runtime and rendering change rather than an instance validation break for ordinary text.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 conclusion strings should generally remain valid R6 markdown values, but generated classes and validators will expose a different primitive type. R6 markdown can be copied to R4 string syntactically, but formatting semantics may be lost or displayed differently.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated model bindings, UI rendering, escaping, and security review for markdown display. Include tests for plain text, markdown syntax, and characters that could be mis-rendered.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A new formatted-conclusion field would have been less disruptive to type signatures but would create duplication. The chosen design centralizes conclusion text.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `conclusion` changed from `string` to `markdown`. Ordinary R4 text remains a JSON string and should normally carry forward, so this is not a hard instance break. The real change is in generated primitive types and display expectations: R6 clients may render or sanitize the conclusion differently. Because conclusions are clinically visible, implementations should notice the change, but marking formatted conclusion text as markdown is a reasonable R6 design.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.conclusion` type is `string` and `isSummary` is false.
R6 snapshot `DiagnosticReport.conclusion` type is `markdown` and `isSummary` is true.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use makes changes to a common clinical text field worth noting, but the wire representation remains string-like and the change supports clearer rendering semantics.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: generated primitive types and renderer/sanitizer assumptions can change; ordinary R4 string values do not become invalid R6 JSON.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `conclusion` as `string` and adding a separate formatted conclusion would preserve old API types, but it creates duplicate conclusion fields. Relying only on prose guidance would also be less computable than the markdown datatype.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium runtime concern and Partial alternative judgment; the concern is real but mostly API/rendering-level rather than an instance break.

findings.title: Summary flags changed for media, conclusion, conclusionCode, and recommendation

oldState.summary: R4 marked `media` and `media.link` as summary; `conclusion` and `conclusionCode` were not summary.

newState.summary: R6 no longer marks `media` or `media.link` as summary; `conclusion`, `conclusionCode`, and new `recommendation` are summary.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Summary flags do not change instance validity, but they can alter REST `_summary`, generated summary views, indexing shortcuts, and client assumptions about which fields appear in lightweight representations.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Clients relying on summary views may omit key media links or newly include conclusion text and recommendations.

justification.inferredGoal: Refocus summary content on conclusions and recommendations rather than media references.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep R4 media summary flags while also adding summary flags for conclusion, conclusionCode, and recommendation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of surfacing conclusions and recommendations in summaries is plausible, but the supplied evidence does not explain why `media` and `media.link` had to be removed from summary. A base design that included both old and new summary fields would have been less disruptive unless there was an unstated payload, privacy, or relevance rationale.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would retain `DiagnosticReport.media` and `DiagnosticReport.media.link` as summary elements for at least a transition while marking conclusion-oriented fields as summary too. This is only a partial alternative because if the R6 goal was specifically to suppress media from summary responses, retaining those flags would not meet that goal and could increase payload or disclosure risk.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old summary behavior but enlarge summary payloads and may conflict with a deliberate decision to exclude media from summaries.

evidence.detail: R4 summary flags differ from R6 for these local elements.
R6 summary flags move emphasis away from media and toward conclusion/recommendation content.

examples.examplesMd: No instance syntax changes are involved; the risk is changed server/client behavior for summary projections.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes which DiagnosticReport fields are marked summary. The most visible shift is that media links fall out of summary while conclusions and recommendations enter summary.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This does not make any old instance invalid. It can make runtime behavior differ if systems depend on FHIR summary flags to shape REST responses or generated lightweight DTOs.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review `_summary` handling, generated summary models, cache population, and UI cards. Do not assume R6 summary responses include media links.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Summary flag changes are inherently behavioral. Backward compatibility could be approximated by server configuration or profiles, but the base flags have changed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The changed `isSummary` flags can alter REST `_summary` results and generated lightweight views: media links are no longer summary, while conclusion-oriented fields and recommendation become summary. That is a visible metadata/API shift, but it does not affect instance validity and is the kind of summary-surface change clients should treat as versioned behavior rather than a stable clinical contract.
keyEvidence: R4 snapshot marks `DiagnosticReport.media` and `DiagnosticReport.media.link` as summary and leaves `conclusion` and `conclusionCode` non-summary.
R6 snapshot marks `media` and `media.link` non-summary, and marks `conclusion`, `conclusionCode`, and `recommendation` as summary.
R4 maturity map checked: DiagnosticReport is FMM 3 and trial-use.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use makes summary behavior relevant for implementations, but this remains metadata/API behavior rather than a wire-format or semantic data loss break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: `_summary` payloads and generated summary views may include or omit different fields; there is no old-valid/new-invalid instance effect.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept media links in summary while adding the new summary fields, but that may conflict with the apparent move away from returning media/document links in compact responses. The compatibility benefit is modest and does not justify a Revisit judgment.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Low impact and Partial alternative judgment; the runtime behavior change is real, but I judge it as no meaningful compatibility problem.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, type, kind, abstract flag, derivation, and DomainResource base definition remain stable.
No common local DiagnosticReport element had a min or max cardinality change. All newly added R6 elements are optional at their top level.
No local DiagnosticReport modifier meaning changed. `DiagnosticReport.status` remains a modifier in both versions; inherited modifierExtension and implicitRules text changes are out of scope.
No local DiagnosticReport slicing changes were found in the compared StructureDefinitions.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value change was found.

The required `status` binding change is reported as a finding. The local `category`, `code`, and `conclusionCode` bindings keep their strength and canonical ValueSet, with description changes only; no live expansions were run for broad non-required bindings.
The only new local DiagnosticReport constraint found is `dgr-1`, reported above. Inherited `dom-*`, `ele-*`, and `ext-*` changes are out of scope for this artifact.
No whole-resource serialization format change was found. Serialization risks are localized to element wire-name or datatype changes reported above.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact maturity/status metadata advanced
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The resource identity and structure base remain stable. Metadata changes from R4 draft/trial-use to R6 active/normative affect governance expectations, not instance validity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Implementers may treat normative R6 behavior as more stable, but should remember the package is still ballot build `6.0.0-ballot4`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Several non-required binding descriptions were refined
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `category` remains example-bound to diagnostic-service-sections, `code` remains preferred-bound to report-codes, and `conclusionCode` remains example-bound to clinical-findings. Binding strength did not increase for these local elements.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The R6 descriptions emphasize HL7 v2 table 0074, LOINC report codes, and SNOMED CT clinical findings. This can influence terminology guidance even without hard validation changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Several definitions and comments were clarified or broadened
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The computable cardinalities and types for these specific elements did not narrow, except where separately reported. The text changes mainly clarify clinically relevant time, encounter association, point-of-care performers, and media as images or data.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review business rules that relied on old prose, especially for encounter timing and performer responsibility.
